fact: The ACE consortium lists Freetown, Sierra Leone as an ACE landing station and says ACE is the first international submarine cable to land in Sierra Leone, in service since 15 December 2012 (page undated; in-service date is the consortium's).

The Conversation Africa (interview) says Sierra Leone, like Liberia, has only one fibre optic cable coming into the country, so its internet traffic stops when that cable breaks; the cable is not named.

fact: ECOWAS says the six countries of the Amilcar Cabral project currently have only one landing station.
Developing Telecoms, citing a Liberian ministry press release, says Sierra Leone currently has only one international subsea connection, via the ACE cable.

The government announcement says a second submarine cable is meant to reduce Sierra Leone's reliance on a single international submarine cable; the second cable, a $45 million project with a new National Cable Consortium, is planned, not in service.
Liberty Online TV reports the Government unveiled plans for a second submarine cable, estimated at US$40 million, as an alternative route after a cable cut in March 2024.
